task_description: Write a method in Dafny to find element at a given index after number of rotations.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method RotatedElement(arr: array<int>, rotations: int, index: int) returns (result: int)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The result should be the element at the specified index after rotating the input array to the left by the given number of rotations
- The input array remains unchanged
- The index is within the valid bounds of the array indices (0 to arr.Length - 1)
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method RotatedElement(arr: array<int>, k: int, n: int) returns (result: int)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The array should have at least one element
    - The index k should be within the array bounds
    - The number of rotations n should be non-negative
    
Dafny specification:
    requires arr.Length > 0
    requires 0 <= k < arr.Length
    requires n >= 0
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The element returned is the element at position k after rotating the array arr to the right by n positions
    
Dafny specification:
    ensures result == arr[(k - n + arr.Length) % arr.Length]
    
Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method RotatedElement(arr: array<int>, k: int, n: int) returns (result: int)
    requires arr.Length > 0
    requires 0 <= k < arr.Length
    requires n >= 0
    ensures result == arr[(k - n + arr.Length) % arr.Length]
{
    var index := (k - n + arr.Length) % arr.Length;
    result := arr[index];
}
```
